headlines.article_text: Ford Motor (F) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Ford Motor reported earnings that beat Wall Street’s estimates but slightly missed on revenue. The Detroit automaker also narrowed its 2026 guidance, raising it at the low end, and said earnings next year will be in line with its results from this year. Ford has been working to recover production of its F-Series pickup trucks after dealing with supplier issues for much of the past year. In this article F Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A close-up view shows a standalone Ford corporate Blue Oval logo monument sign at a vehicle dealership in Santaquin, Utah, United States, on August 30, 2026. Charles-McClintock Wilson | Nurphoto | Getty Images DETROIT — Ford Motor expects earnings next year will be roughly in line with the automaker's anticipated results this year, the company said Wednesday as it reported mixed results for the third quarter. The Detroit automaker beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations but slightly missed revenue estimates. The company has been working to stabilize production of its F-Series pickup trucks after dealing with supplier issues for much of the past year. "This quarter's results reflect deliberate actions to improve profitability and deliver consistent financial returns," Ford CFO Sherry House told reporters during a call Wednesday. Here's how Ford performed in the third quarter, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG: Earnings per share: 49 cents adjusted vs. 40 cents expected Automotive revenue: $46.08 billion vs. $46.24 billion expected The Detroit automaker also narrowed its 2026 guidance to adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of between $10.5 billion and $11 billion, compared with a previous outlook of $10 billion to $11 billion. Ford maintained its adjusted free cash flow guidance for this year of between $6 billion and $7 billion. House also said the company expects 2027 profitability to be roughly in line with this year's results, citing several offsetting factors in production issues this year as well as rising commodity costs. House noted a $1.3 billion tariff refund during the first quarter of this year was largely offset by additional costs from alternative aluminum sourcing that the company does not expect to have next year, leveling out the year-over-year comparison. She also said production of its F-Series Super Duty trucks in Canada in 2027 will make up for lost production it's expecting at its F-150 factories to retool for new models. "Next year will be the third year on our journey of increasing and improving our warranty and material cost savings, and that's getting extended to structural costs throughout the company as well in terms of savings," House said. Ahead of the results, Wall Street analysts were mixed about whether Ford would be able to maintain profits in 2027. The company has multiple efforts that will add to costs next year: It's rolling out several new or redesigned models, including its next-generation EV and Canada-produced pickups, and is enhancing its energy business that it announced earlier this year. The missed revenue for the third quarter was a result of each of the automaker's main business units – which are broken into Blue traditional operations, Pro fleet and Model e electric vehicle segments – underperforming compared with Wall Street's expectations, according to StreetAccount. As part of its modified guidance, Ford said it now expects pre-tax earnings of its Ford Blue unit to be $5.5 billion, which is at the high end of a previous guidance. It's also anticipating EBIT of about $7 billion for the year for Ford Pro and Ford Model e losses of about $4 billion. Its Ford Credit unit is expected to record about $2.8 billion in EBIT for 2026. Ford's overall revenue, which includes its credit segment, was off roughly 2% compared with the third quarter of last year, to $49.5 billion. Its net income also was off $400 million from a year earlier to $2 billion, while adjusted earnings before interest and taxes were up slightly year-over-year to $2.7 billion. Ford's 2025 third-quarter results included $47.19 billion in automotive revenue, net income of $2.4 billion and earnings per share of 45 cents adjusted. headlines.article_text: Oracle stock pops on forecast for 35% average growth through 2030 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Oracle shares jumped after the software company issued a revenue forecast of $225 billion for fiscal 2030, implying 35% average annual growth. Analysts polled by LSEG expected growth of 8% in fiscal 2027, followed by significant acceleration over the next two years. The company also said it committed to limit additional funding for fiscal 2027 through 2030 to $20 billion, expecting that total to be divided equally between equity and debt. In this article ORCL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Oracle co-CEO Caly Magouryk, speaking at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas on Oct. 27th, 2026. CNBC Oracle shares jumped 11% on Wednesday after the software company issued a revenue forecast of $225 billion for fiscal 2030, implying 35% average annual growth, and said it will limit additional fundraising over that stretch to $20 billion. At its investor day, Oracle said that, as part of its financing plan for fiscal 2027 through 2030, the amount raised will be divided equally between equity and debt. "Vendor financing, customer-provided hardware and customer prepayments are expected to reduce upfront cash requirements through the transition to positive free cash flow," Oracle said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Analysts polled by LSEG expected revenue growth of 8% in fiscal 2027, followed by significant acceleration over the next two years. They're projecting revenue in fiscal 2030 of $224.2 billion. Prior to Wednesday, Oracle had lost about one-third of its value this year on concern that rising interest rates and the company's hefty debt load will make its artificial intelligence buildout too costly. Oracle has issued $117 billion in long-term debt and is clinging to an investment-grade credit rating of BBB-, the lowest level of investment grade above junk, according to S&P. Long known as a giant in enterprise software, Oracle jumped into the AI infrastructure game in a major way last year to try and compete with the hyperscalers like Google and Amazon while providing capacity to OpenAI. Its capital expenditures more than doubled to $55.7 billion in fiscal 2026, and are expected to jump another 65% this fiscal year to $91.9 billion, according to FactSet. Oracle needs revenue expansion from its buildout to cover the soaring costs. The company said its operating margin in fiscal 2030 will top 40%. Oracle also said it will turn free cash flow positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 and reach more than $30 billion in free cash flow the following year. Analysts expect negative free cash flow of $35 billion this fiscal year and a similar number next year, according to FactSet. The spread on Oracle's five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, currently sits at 277 basis points after reaching about 320 basis points earlier this month. It's up almost 100% this year. —CNBC's Michelle Fox and Jordan Novet contributed to this report. Alex Wong | Getty Images Three media outlets that President Donald Trump banned from the White House in September, only to have a federal judge's order restore much of their access, amended their lawsuit Wednesday, seeking to regain full access to serve in a press pool for other reporters in the Oval Office and Air Force One . The amended civil complaint says that since the judge ordered the White House to allow MS NOW , CNN and Politico journalists into the White House, the White House has blocked those outlets from performing pool functions they long have conducted. The press pool routinely serves as a key source of information for the public about what a president does or says. The amended complaint sets the stage for a court fight over whether a president, because of how he or she feels about how a media outlet covers them, can block access to individual media outlets or reporters from areas of the White House that other journalists have access. "The President's ban and the White House's continued exclusion of Plaintiffs from certain [areas] are unlawful retaliation for protected First Amendment activity," the amended complaint in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C. says. The initial ban and subsequent barring of the outlets "from certain White House press areas "brazenly discriminates against Plaintiffs based on their perceived editorial viewpoint; the White House is expressly excluding CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO because the President dislikes the content of their coverage," the suit says. headlines.article_text: FTC demands Walmart and others hand over data on personalized pricing Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Andrew Ferguson speaks during the Semafor World Economy Summit 2025 at Conrad Washington on April 23, 2025 in Washington, DC. Kayla Bartkowski | Getty Images The Federal Trade Commission is demanding information from Walmart , Uber and seven other companies on whether and how they use consumers' personal data such as location, browsing history and income to set individual prices, wages and job offers, a senior FTC official told Reuters on Wednesday. The FTC is flexing its consumer protection powers ahead of the U.S. congressional elections next week, as voters consistently rank the cost of living as the most important issue. Target , along with app services Lyft , DoorDash and Instacart, and airlines Delta , United , JetBlue , are also receiving demands, the official said. The FTC will use the information to eventually publish a study to help inform regulators and lawmakers about personalized pricing and wage setting practices. The advance of algorithmic pricing technology, including tools that incorporate AI, has fueled concern that companies are able to set prices for shoppers on an individual basis in order to extract the maximum price each shopper would be willing to pay. Personalized pricing strategies are difficult to observe from the outside, because they serve different prices to different people. The FTC study aims to fill in that knowledge gap, demanding comprehensive information about the tools, strategies, and data companies use as well as how they affect prices, wages and job offers. Efforts by state lawmakers to ban personalized pricing, along with the use of algorithms to individually tailor wages, have taken off in recent years. The National Retail Federation has criticized the laws and defended retailers' use of data-driven discounts as a means of incentivizing loyalty. FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson has said personalizing pricing could violate consumer protection laws where consumers do not expect it and that companies should expect enforcement. After the FTC called for public comment, hundreds of commenters urged the FTC to ban the practice outright. The FTC has said it does not have the authority to issue a blanket prohibition against the practice. headlines.title: Apple brings touch to the Mac, reversing years-old stance on touchscreen laptop
headlines.summary: Apple announces a new touchscreen laptop, the company's third major launch under new CEO John Ternus.
headlines.article_text: MacBook Pro: Apple brings touch to the Mac Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points The launch signifies the growing strategic importance of the Mac to Apple, despite it generating less revenue than the iPhone. The move comes as global PC shipments fall and Apple faces pressure from rising memory costs and higher computer prices. Touchscreens have not typically driven laptop purchases, making Apple's software changes and developer strategy central to whether the feature catches on. In this article AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT German-Russian record producer and DJ Zedd, at left, and Apple CEO John Ternus look at the new M6 14-inch MacBook Pro during the Apple Experience LA event in Los Angeles, Oct. 28, 2026. Frederic J. Brown | Afp | Getty Images Apple on Wednesday announced its first laptop with a touch screen, which it is calling MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display. Apple said that the laptop has a new display, using OLED technology, that offers more brightness, better colors and wider viewing angles. It's using Apple's M5 Pro or Max chips, and Apple said on Wednesday that it's lighter than Apple's current pro laptops. It's still an Apple laptop, and is running MacOS, not a version of the iPhone or iPad operating system. In a video, Apple showed users swiping on the screen to manipulate videos or images. It also has a glowing Apple logo on the laptop's lid. The new laptop will go on sale on Nov. 6 and the 14-inch version will start at $2,899. The 16-inch version will cost at least $3,399. Both are notable price increases from existing models. This is Apple's third major product launch under new CEO John Ternus, signaling a faster cadence for hardware releases. It's also a major reversal for Apple, which has resisted putting touchscreens on its laptops for decades as some Windows machines gained the feature. "Yes, for the very first time, we are bringing touch to the Mac," Ternus said in live remarks to media and analysts in Los Angeles. The new MacBook Pro comes at a time when the laptop market has been going through one of its worst slumps ever. Overall shipments are expected to be down 11% this year. Analysts say the AI-driven global market shortage of memory has contributed to higher laptop prices, which has hurt sales and demand. In the third quarter, total PC shipments dropped 20% on a year-over-year basis, according to market researcher IDC. Apple's own shipments fell 11% during the quarter, according to the estimate. Attendees play with the new Touchscreen MacBook Pro (OLED) during the Apple Experience LA in Los Angeles on Oct. 28, 2026. Frederic J. Brown | AFP | Getty Images Even Apple's not immune to rising memory prices, after former CEO Tim Cook warned this summer that the situation around memory prices was "unsustainable." Nearly all Macs got price hikes this year. Mac Minis introduced in August got a $300 bump, for example. The announcement caps a busy two months of product launches under Ternus. Apple also introduced new iMac and MacBook Pro models with M6 chips this week, after price hikes to the lineup totaling several hundred dollars in June. Apple introduced an iPad Mini on Monday that starts at $699, $100 more than its predecessor. In September, Apple released new iPhones, including its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo. It also revealed a new smart speaker with a display called HomeView that uses a redesigned version of Siri to answer a broader range of questions. The launch signifies the growing strategic importance of the Mac to Apple, despite it generating less revenue than the iPhone. In the most recent quarter, Apple reported $10.35 billion in Mac sales, or just under 10% of the company's total revenue. But many software developers swear by the Mac, and it remains the only supported platform to develop iPhone apps. And in recent months, Apple has highlighted its chips and memory architecture to make the case that its computers are the best fit for local or edge AI that runs on a device, instead of the cloud. Meta's AI model developer team bought hundreds of Mac Minis this year to test agents, for example. And Apple notably teamed up with Meta earlier this month to make an announcement that large, nearly frontier models can run on clusters of Macs connected with high-speed cabling, allowing developers to run agentic code without paying Anthropic or OpenAI. Read more CNBC tech news Amazon’s anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI Chart: Anthropic’s cash pile towers over nearly every U.S. company Google alters its cloud playbook, enlisting partners to sell more AI chips A guide to some of the biggest risks in Anthropic's IPO prospectus Apple has had a historical resistance to touchscreen laptops — software chief Craig Federighi explained in 2018 that the ergonomics would fatigue users. "We make the world's best touch computer on an iPad. It's totally optimized for that. And the Mac is totally optimized for indirect input. We haven't really felt a reason to change that," Ternus, then Apple's senior VP of hardware engineering, told The Wall Street Journal's Joanna Stern in 2021. Ternus has been working on Macs since he joined the company and was credited along with silicon chief Johny Srouji as the leader of Apple's effort to get Macs running on Apple's chips, not Intel's. Apple credited Ternus' work on Mac in its official CEO transition statement . That may be why Ternus in his early days as CEO will be the executive to backtrack on a long-running Apple design philosophy. Touchscreen laptops have been available on Windows machines for a long time, but they're just another feature, not a selling point behind most purchasing decisions, Ryan Reith, IDC VP for worldwide device trackers, said. Only 17% of notebook PCs shipped globally this year will have touchscreens, according to IDC data. Touchscreen laptops also have a slightly lower average selling price than non-touchscreen notebooks. Hardware technology hasn't been the limiting factor for Apple merging its desktop and mobile interfaces, he added, and Apple could have been waiting to launch a touchscreen laptop until it could present a good user experience and perfect its software after attempts to make its iPad more like a laptop. "This is really a user interface and software thing," Reith said.
